title: Full-width pointer-events:auto overlay band swallows touch taps meant for the player — gate it to (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)
trigger: A shadow-DOM overlay band/row covering part of a video has pointer-events:auto (e.g. as a drag surface), and on touch devices taps into that band never reach the player — play/pause/toggle-controls appear dead under the covered region
principle: pointer-events:auto on a wide overlay container consumes every pointer hit inside its box — the host page below never sees the tap. On desktop this is survivable (users click elsewhere, and a big grab band is a deliberate affordance); on touch, tap-to-toggle-controls is THE primary player gesture, so a dead band reads as 'the site is broken'. Scope the container's pointer-events:auto to '@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)' so coarse-pointer devices get pointer-events:none and taps fall through to the player natively — no synthetic re-dispatch needed. Keep the drag affordance on touch by letting the gesture start from a real interactive child (e.g. the subtitle text block) with a small movement threshold + deferred setPointerCapture, so a short tap still resolves as a normal click (word lookup / text selection) and only a real drag captures the pointer. Hit-test inside shadow DOM via shadowRoot.elementFromPoint — document.elementFromPoint retargets to the host.

cases.context: SubtitlePanels .root band (full video width, ~74px, pointer-events:auto + touch-action:none) existed to drag-reposition subtitles. On a 203px-tall mobile YouTube player it swallowed ~36% of the tap area — users could not toggle the native controls scrim at all and reported 'lớp che không thể thao tác'.

Verification probe: document.elementFromPoint inside the video rect returned #cell-subtitle-root (retargeted from the .root shadow child); shadowRoot.elementFromPoint revealed the real hit (band vs button vs subtitle .layer).
cases.bad:
// assumed host pointer-events:none meant click-through — but a shadow child with
// pointer-events:auto still intercepts; document.elementFromPoint only shows the host
